dedupe_keys.name: helsinki 3d city models 3d mesh semantic city model and energy and climate atlas

description: Helsinki's 3D city models, which the city also calls its digital twin, are a virtual rendering of the city's environment, operations and changing conditions, combining IT services, open data and continuously updated information. The 3D mesh models are built from summer aerial photographs turned into textured triangle meshes and show all stationary objects, including buildings, vehicles and ships, and can be viewed in a browser to see the city change over the years. The Energy and Climate Atlas built on the city model has sections on building energy data, simulated heating demand, solar potential for every roof and wall surface and geothermal potential, with open data downloadable like other Helsinki Region Infoshare data; the Stadi3D tool offers downloads, and a Minecraft version covers the city. Coverage: the City of Helsinki and part of the region. Access: viewers and download tools linked from the page, updated September 2026. Licence: open data; terms on the Helsinki Region Infoshare service were not read. Caveats: the mesh is only as accurate as the photographs, and reflective or moving surfaces are poorly modelled; the Atlas is still in development. Simulation uses are city-scale energy, solar and heat studies and a base for urban digital twins. Related records: the OGC CityGML standard and other city 3D models.
